definitions.gloss: burglary of an empty house; sneak thief; prowler
definitions.explanation: Breaking into and stealing from a house or building while the occupants are away. Also refers to the person who commits this crime.

examples.japanese: {空|あ}き{巣|す}に{入|はい}られた。
この{地域|ちいき}では{空|あ}き{巣|す}の{被害|ひがい}が{増|ふ}えている。
examples.english: Burglaries have been increasing in this area.

examples.japanese: {旅行中|りょこうちゅう}に{空|あ}き{巣|す}に{入|はい}られないよう、{戸締|とじ}まりを{確認|かくにん}した。
examples.english: I checked the locks to make sure we wouldn't be burgled while traveling.

notes:
USAGE:
Can refer to both the act of burglary and the burglar themselves. The key nuance is that the crime targets an empty dwelling—the occupants are not home.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {空|あ}き{巣|す}に{入|はい}られる (to be burgled)
- {空|あ}き{巣|す}{被害|ひがい} (burglary damage)
- {空|あ}き{巣|す}{対策|たいさく} (anti-burglary measures)
- {空|あ}き{巣|す}{狙|ねら}い (targeting empty houses)

WORD FORMATION:
{空|あ}き (empty, vacant) + {巣|す} (nest, den). Literally "empty nest," referring to a home left unoccupied.
